title: Development Levy
description: Area boys want their levy, Nne is in the hospital, and a danfo driver needs a second pair of hands.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Tuesday. Ike is at the wharf. You are alone with the till when four boys walk in, the way weather walks in.

beats.speaker: scatter
beats.text: Oga Ike no dey? No problem. Development levy. Ten thousand. The road you are using, somebody developed it.

beats.speaker: ngozi
beats.text: (from across the road, not looking up) Don't pay from the till. Ike will say you stole it. Don't refuse either. They come back at night.

options.text: Pay from the till. It's Ike's road too.
Send a boy running for Professor.
options.lockedText: You don't know the old agbero well enough

won.toast: Scatter limps off. The whole market saw. The whole market will talk.

lost.toast: They take ₦5,000 from your pocket and leave the till alone. Strange mercy.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: (arriving slowly, on purpose) Scatter. Your mother sells fish at Ẹ̀bútẹ́. Shall I go and greet her? Tell her what her son does on Tuesdays?

beats.speaker: scatter
beats.text: (after a long time) Prof... e no reach that level. (They leave. Scatter salutes, badly.)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Evening. Uncle Dozie calls. Uncle Dozie never calls.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: Your mother fell at the stream this morning. Her blood pressure, the nurse says. The hospital wants ₦25,000 deposit before they will even look at her properly.

beats.speaker: uncleDozie
beats.text: I don't have it. You are the Lagos man now.

variants.text: She was carrying oil for the women you paid. She told everybody the money came from Lagos. Now Lagos must come again.

options.text: Send it. All of it. Whatever it takes.
Ask Ike for an advance on your wages.
"Uncle, you are there. Handle it. I will refund you."

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: (sending the money from his phone without looking up) Twenty-five. You owe me thirty. Lagos interest. Don't argue, I'm being kind.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The money you saved from your first pay is still in your sock. You think about it for a long time.

beats.objective: Walk off the worry. Go under the bridge, where the danfos sleep.

beats.speaker: biodun
beats.text: (lying on the roof of his danfo, eating groundnuts) You are Ike's boy. The one who looks at the sky like he's owed money by it.

beats.speaker: biodun
beats.text: My conductor ran away to Ghana. Saturdays I need someone to drive the evening run while I count. You can drive?

beats.speaker: biodun
beats.text: Ten thousand a Saturday. You crash it, you buy it.

options.text: "I drove the quarry truck for two years. Give me the keys."
"Not now, oga. Ike owns my Saturdays."

done.toast: Bíọ́dún counts the fares twice and gives you ₦10,000. "You drive like an old woman. Good. Old women don't crash."

beats.title: Development Levy
beats.summary: You learned what the road costs, who you call when the road sends its boys, and how far ₦25,000 is from a hospital bed in Nkwọ-Agụụ.
